method: Footprint analysis of the code path (per item and per batch), checked against Soroban per-transaction limits. Re-measure with `stellar contract invoke --sim-only` against a 16-item batch and update `budgets/baseline.json` when the code path changes.

per_item.read_entries_notes: WorkItem key + attestation-registry AttestationSequence, RevokedThrough and the latest Attestation entry. Records with long, interleaved version history (up to MAX_HISTORY=10) read more; such batches fail at simulation and must be split.

per_batch_fixed.read_entries_notes: instance entries of incentive-pool, attester-registry and attestation-registry + EpochApproved; plus 1 attester-registry read per distinct attester (memoized in-call)

justification: 16 items keep writes at 18/50 and typical reads at 84/100 even with every item from a distinct attester; 32 items would exceed the read limit (148).

disburse.method: Footprint analysis of the code path (per item and per batch), checked against Soroban per-transaction limits. `disburse` shares the same guard function as `claim` (caps, eligibility, replay protection) and adds a payout-binding read plus a push-mode flag check per item. Re-measure with `stellar contract invoke --sim-only` against a 16-item batch and update `budgets/baseline.json` when the code path changes.

per_item.read_entries_notes: Same reads as `claim` (WorkItem key + attestation-registry AttestationSequence, RevokedThrough and latest Attestation entry) plus the attester's payout binding entry and its push-mode flag. Records with long, interleaved version history (up to MAX_HISTORY=10) read more; such batches fail at simulation and must be split.
per_item.events_notes: One audit event per disbursed item, matching the per-item audit event emitted by `claim`

per_batch_fixed.read_entries_notes: instance entries of incentive-pool, attester-registry and attestation-registry + EpochApproved; plus 1 attester-registry read per distinct attester (memoized in-call)

disburse.justification: 16 items keep writes at 18/50 and typical reads at 100/100 even with every item from a distinct attester (4 fixed + 16 * 6 = 100). This is the tightest batch that fits the read limit; 17 items would exceed it (106). The bound is therefore derived from the read-entry budget: max_batch_disbursements = floor((100 - 4) / 6) = 16. Batches with long attestation histories read more per item and must be split.
